sections.heading: What Is Low-E Glass and Why Does It Matter?
sections.body: Low-E, or low-emissivity, glass features a microscopic metallic coating applied to the surface of the glass that reflects radiant heat while still allowing natural light to pass through. This coating minimizes the transfer of heat in both directions — keeping heat out during hot summers and retaining warmth during cold winters. For properties in Herndon, where temperatures fluctuate significantly between seasons, Low-E glass is a practical upgrade that enhances comfort and reduces the strain on HVAC systems. The coating is nearly invisible to the naked eye, so you retain clear sightlines and natural daylight without sacrificing thermal performance. Whether you are replacing a single failed sealed unit or retrofitting an entire building facade, Low-E glass offers a meaningful improvement over standard clear glass. Our team explains all available options so you can make an informed choice that fits your property's specific needs and budget.

sections.heading: Residential Low-E Glass Replacement in Herndon Neighborhoods
sections.body: Homeowners in established Herndon neighborhoods such as Worldgate and the communities surrounding Runnymede Park frequently reach out to us for Low-E glass replacement in casement windows, sliding glass doors, double-hung windows, and patio doors. Our residential team takes care to protect interior finishes and landscaping during the replacement process, leaving your home clean and tidy when the work is done. sections.heading: Low-E Glass Options: Soft Coat vs. Hard Coat
sections.body: Not all Low-E glass is the same, and selecting the right type depends on your climate goals, building orientation, and budget. There are two primary manufacturing categories: soft-coat (also called sputtered) Low-E and hard-coat (also called pyrolytic) Low-E. Soft-coat Low-E glass generally provides a higher level of thermal performance and is the more commonly specified option for double- and triple-pane insulated glass units. Hard-coat Low-E is more durable when exposed and is sometimes used in specific single-pane or secondary glazing applications. Our glazing specialists walk you through the differences and help identify which product makes the most sense for your specific project. We source quality glass from reputable suppliers and ensure each unit is manufactured to the correct specifications for your frames. Herndon property owners can count on us to recommend solutions honestly, without overselling products that do not match the actual needs of the job.

faq.q: How do I know if my Low-E glass needs to be replaced?
faq.a: The most common sign that an insulated Low-E glass unit has failed is visible fogging, condensation, or a hazy film between the two panes of glass. This occurs when the hermetic seal around the unit breaks down, allowing moisture-laden air to enter the space between the panes. Once the seal fails, the unit cannot be cleaned or repaired — it must be replaced. You may also notice increased drafts, cold spots near windows, or a visible discoloration in the glass. If you see any of these signs at your Herndon property, contact us for an assessment.

faq.q: Can Low-E glass be installed in my existing window frames?
faq.a: In many cases, yes. If your existing frames are in good structural condition, we can often replace just the glass unit itself — called the insulated glass unit or IGU — without replacing the entire window or door assembly. We take precise measurements of your existing units and source replacement Low-E IGUs manufactured to those specifications. This approach is typically more cost-effective than full window replacement and results in minimal disruption to your home or business. Our team will assess your frames during the estimate visit and advise you on whether a glass-only replacement is appropriate.
